samples.summary: printDryRun's dot-segment backstop only catches literal `.`/`..`, not the percent-encoded spellings the URL parser also resolves
samples.evidence: `assertNoDotSegments` compares each segment against exactly `'.'` and `'..'`. The WHATWG URL parser treats `%2e`, `%2E`, `.%2e`, `%2e%2e` (case-insensitive) as single/double-dot path segments too, so a future call site that interpolated an id of `%2e%2e` raw would pass this backstop and the printed URL would still normalize one level up — the exact failure the guard exists to prevent. `seg()` itself is safe (it encodes the `%`), so only this backstop is incomplete, i.e. it does not actually enforce the invariant its doc comment claims ("after encoding, no segment of `path` can be `.` or `..`").

samples.summary: clampUpstreamText discards any upstream message that merely *starts with* `<`, losing actionable text for non-HTML messages
samples.evidence: `if (!trimmed || trimmed.startsWith('<')) return null;` — the heuristic is "first char is `<` ⇒ HTML document". A legitimate backend/class-validator message such as `"<title> must be a non-empty string"` or `"<empty> is not a valid range"` is silently replaced by a bare `HTTP <status>`, dropping the only text that says what went wrong — the very regression the surrounding comment says it is fixing on the non-envelope path.

samples.summary: safeEnvelope's oversized branch invents a `message` field the upstream envelope did not have
samples.evidence: In the small-body branch, `error.message` is only set when `'message' in body.error` (line 164). In the oversized branch the fallback is `{ error: { code, message: error.message ?? `HTTP ${status}` } }` — so an envelope like `{error:{code:'X'}, debug:<6KB>}` gains a synthetic `message: "HTTP 500"` while the same envelope under 4000 bytes emits no `message` at all. The output shape for the same logical input depends only on body size.

samples.summary: `runFilesDownload` can report a success status as an error message ("HTTP 200")
samples.evidence: The condition is `if (!res.ok || !res.bytes)`, but `upstreamErrorJson(res)` renders `HTTP ${res.status}`. When the response was OK yet carried no bytes, the emitted envelope reads `{code:'HTTP_ERROR', message:'HTTP 200'}` — a message that tells the caller the request succeeded while exiting 1. Previously this path printed a status-free `HTTP_ERROR`, so the change made the misleading status visible.

samples.summary: `seg()` makes the synchronous `fileUrl()` throw during React render for a `.`/`..` route param, crashing the view instead of showing not-found
samples.evidence: `fileUrl` is called synchronously in render paths (`packages/frontend/src/app/files/pdf-collab.tsx:139`, `packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:726`) with a router param. React Router percent-decodes params, so navigating to `/f/%2E%2E` yields `documentId === '..'`; `seg` then throws `Invalid path segment` synchronously inside render, which unmounts to an error boundary / blank screen rather than the normal "document not found" handling that a rejected fetch would have produced. Every other `seg()` call site is inside an async function where the throw becomes a rejection the caller already handles.

samples.summary: `isAllowedHost` cannot express an IPv6 or default-port allow-list entry the way the docs describe
samples.evidence: `url.host` omits the port for default 80/443 and brackets IPv6 (`[fd00::1]:9000`), while `parseAllowedHosts` lowercases/trims raw text. So an operator entry `10.0.0.5:80` never matches `http://10.0.0.5/` (host is `10.0.0.5`), and an entry `fd00::1` never matches `[fd00::1]` — the documented `host` / `host:port` contract silently fails for those, and the export is refused with a message pointing at an env var the operator already set.

samples.summary: `assertResolvedHostIsPublic` throws an unhandled TypeError for a relative URL when called outside `guard`
samples.evidence: `const url = new URL(resolved);` is unguarded, unlike `assertFetchableImageUrl` which wraps the same call in try/catch and reports a readable refusal. The function is exported, so any caller that invokes it without first calling `assertFetchableImageUrl` (the docs present the two as a pair, but nothing enforces the order) gets a raw `TypeError: Invalid URL` instead of the documented refusal.

mergedFrom.summary: Redirect response bodies are never consumed or cancelled in the manual-redirect loop

finding.summary: `redirect: 'manual'` may produce an opaque-redirect response, breaking every redirecting image URL
finding.evidence: `const res = await fetchImpl(current, { redirect: 'manual' });` then `REDIRECT_STATUSES.has(res.status) ? res.headers.get('location') : null`. Per the Fetch Standard, redirect mode "manual" yields an *opaque-redirect filtered response*: `status === 0`, empty header list, null body. If the Node runtime the CLI ships on implements that filtering (undici has historically gone back and forth on this), `res.status` is 0, `location` is null, `res.ok` is false, and the loop throws `Image fetch failed: 0  for <url>` — so a CDN/S3 `302` (the normal case for stored blobs) makes `docs export`/`slides export` fail instead of following the hop. Every redirect test in `packages/cli/test/image-fetcher.test.ts` injects a hand-built `Response` with a real 302 status and headers, so a stub can never surface this; nothing exercises the real `fetch`.

verdict.reason: The finding claims an opaque-redirect response (status 0) falls through to `Image fetch failed: 0`, breaking every redirecting image URL. That path is explicitly guarded: image-fetcher.ts:326-331 checks `if (res.status === 0)` immediately after the fetch and before the `REDIRECT_STATUSES`/`res.ok` logic, throwing a dedicated "Image fetch got an opaque redirect ... this runtime's fetch hides redirect targets" error. The reviewer's quoted evidence omits this guard, and the claimed error string is unreachable. The claim that "a stub can never surface this; nothing exercises the real fetch" is also wrong: test/image-fetcher.test.ts:416-433 injects `Response.error()` (a filtered response, since `Response` cannot be constructed with status 0) and asserts the `/opaque redirect/` message. Finally the premise about the shipping runtime fails: packages/cli/package.json:10-12 sets `"engines": {"node": ">=20"}`, where undici returns the real 3xx plus `Location` for `redirect: 'manual'` (opaque-redirect filtering is a browser rule), so a CDN/S3 302 is followed through the per-hop guard at lines 333-357. The lessons doc at docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-lessons.md:106-111 records this was verified on the supported runtime, not assumed. No correctness defect: the described failure mode is both guarded and tested.
